items.title: A 5-character token yields "…" plus its last 4 characters
covers: AC2: token longer than 4 characters (just above the limit)
items.reason: AC2 switches rule at 4 characters; 5 is the shortest token that shows its end. Guards an off-by-one (`>=` vs `>`) that would hide the hint or show the whole token.

items.title: A 4-character token yields "…" alone, never the whole token
covers: AC2: token with 1 to 4 characters shows "…" alone (upper edge)
items.reason: AC2 forbids showing a whole token; with a 4-character token "the last 4 characters" is the whole token, so this is the edge where a naive implementation leaks it.

items.title: A 1-character token yields "…" alone
covers: AC2: token with 1 to 4 characters shows "…" alone (lower edge)
items.reason: Lower edge of AC2's 1–4 range: one character is still a token (not "no token"), so the hint must be `"…"`, not `null` and not the character itself.

items.title: A subscription registered without a token has tokenHint null
covers: AC2: tokenHint is null when the subscription has no token
items.reason: AC2's third branch. The Webhooks API accepts a POST without a token (only the client UI requires one), so such rows exist and must not get `"…"` or crash the mapping.

items.title: A subscription registered with an empty token has tokenHint null
covers: AC2: 0-character token is outside 1–4, treated as no token
items.reason: Just below AC2's 1–4 range: an empty string is not a 1–4 character token, so the literal reading (and the recorded decision) is "no token" → `null`, not `"…"`.

subject: HINT-1
reason: Council (testPlan, blockOn any, pass 9/10): not passed; opus 8/10, sol 7/10; 3 finding(s) stand, 1 note(s).

items.reason: AC5 says the registered token is still the token the Webhooks API sends with each webhook call. Only storage is checked (TC-HINT-1-14); delivery is in Open questions because it 'needs an order to reach OrderPaid on the test stack'. It doesn't: OrderStatusChangedToPaidIntegrationEventHandler only calls retriever.GetSubscriptionsOfType(OrderPaid) and sender.SendAll, and the functional fixture runs real RabbitMQ and already swaps services. Add a functional case: register (POST /api/webhooks/, X-Test-User fresh, token 'fake-token-for-tests-9z8y', url 'https://receiver.test/webhook', event OrderPaid) -> 201; publish an OrderStatusChangedToPaidIntegrationEvent (or resolve and invoke the handler) with the HttpClient primary handler replaced by a recording handler; expect exactly one POST to https://receiver.test/webhook whose X-eshop-whtoken header equals 'fake-token-for-tests-9z8y' (the full token, not its hint).

AC5 explicitly requires the entered token to be sent with webhook calls. Checking its database value does not verify the outgoing header, and this defined requirement cannot be deferred as an open question. Explicitly map reusable sender coverage, such as SenderPostsPayloadAndTokenToEveryReceiver, alongside TC-HINT-1-14, or plan an observable receiver assertion that X-eshop-whtoken equals the registered token.

The expected recorded argument and invocation count are state inside ConfigurableGrantUrlTester, not a documented public interface. Replace that assertion with an observable HTTP grant exchange: a controlled receiver verifies the exact X-eshop-whtoken header and returns the required grant response; assert POST 201 and the unchanged database token.

'the grant tester was called once with token ...' depends on a recorder that is a singleton shared by every test on the functional host (ConfigurableGrantUrlTester is registered AddSingleton). State that the case checks exactly one recorded call for grant URL https://receiver.test/check and hook URL https://receiver.test/webhook made during this test (or that the recorder is reset per test), so two engineers write the same assertion.
